obligations.summary: Market surveillance authorities must carry out an evaluation of an AI system's classification when they have sufficient reason to consider that a provider-classified non-high-risk AI system is indeed high-risk, based on Article 6(3) conditions and Commission guidelines.

Where an evaluation finds an AI system to be high-risk, the market surveillance authority must without undue delay require the provider to take all necessary actions to bring the system into compliance and take appropriate corrective action within a prescribed period.

Where use of the AI system is not restricted to its national territory, the market surveillance authority must without undue delay inform the Commission and other Member States of the evaluation results and required corrective actions.

The provider must ensure all necessary action is taken to bring the AI system into compliance with the requirements and obligations of the Regulation within the period prescribed by the market surveillance authority, or face fines under Article 99.
The provider must ensure all appropriate corrective action is taken in respect of all concerned AI systems it has made available on the Union market.
Where the provider does not take adequate corrective action within the prescribed period, the procedures set out in Article 79(5) to (9) shall apply.

Where the market surveillance authority establishes that the provider intentionally misclassified an AI system as non-high-risk to circumvent Chapter III Section 2 requirements, the provider shall be subject to fines under Article 99.

Market surveillance authorities may perform appropriate checks when monitoring the application of this Article, taking into account information stored in the EU database referred to in Article 71, in accordance with Article 11 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
